mcqs.question: Which property would you choose to separate a set of objects into those that are attracted to a magnet and those that are not?
mcqs.explanation: Magnetism determines whether an object is attracted to a magnet, making it the appropriate property for classifying items as magnetic or non‑magnetic. Color, size, and taste do not affect magnetic attraction.

mcqs.question: If you sort a collection of objects by their ability to conduct electricity, which two groups will you obtain?
mcqs.explanation: Sorting by electrical conductivity separates materials into conductors (which allow electricity to flow) and insulators (which do not). The other pairings are based on different properties.

mcqs.learning_point: Creating groups using more than one property
mcqs.question: Which statement correctly describes grouping using two properties?

options.B: Grouping by color and texture together

mcqs.answer: Grouping by color and texture together
mcqs.explanation: Using two properties means considering both color and texture at the same time to form groups. Options A, C, and D each rely on a single property.

mcqs.learning_point: Explaining why a material belongs to a group
mcqs.question: Why is wood placed in the group of materials that are combustible?

options.A: Because it is a good conductor of electricity

mcqs.explanation: Wood burns readily, so it belongs to the group of combustible materials. The other options describe unrelated properties.

mcqs.learning_point: Using classification to identify suitable materials
mcqs.question: Which material would be most suitable for making a spoon used to eat hot soup?
mcqs.explanation: Metal is strong, safe for food, and conducts heat, making it ideal for a soup spoon. Plastic may melt, glass can break, and wood is less durable and can absorb liquids.

mcqs.question: You have a mixed pile of objects and need to separate those that will stick to a magnet. Which property should you use for classification?
mcqs.explanation: Magnetism is the property that determines whether an object is attracted to a magnet, allowing you to separate magnetic from non‑magnetic items. Color, weight, and texture do not affect magnetic attraction.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is FALSE about grouping objects using a single property?

options.A: Objects can be grouped by a single property such as color.
options.B: Grouping by one property always gives groups that are scientifically useful.
options.D: A group can contain items that share the chosen property.

mcqs.answer: Grouping by one property always gives groups that are scientifically useful.
mcqs.explanation: Statement B is false because a single property may not always produce scientifically meaningful groups; the relevance of the property depends on the context. The other statements correctly describe aspects of grouping.

mcqs.learning_point: Creating groups using more than one property
mcqs.question: To separate kitchen items into groups that are (i) magnetic and (ii) non‑magnetic, and also (i) metal and (ii) non‑metal, which combination of properties should be used?
mcqs.explanation: Using both magnetism and material type (metal vs non‑metal) allows you to create four distinct groups: magnetic metal, non‑magnetic metal, magnetic non‑metal, and non‑magnetic non‑metal. The other property pairs are unrelated to the required classification.
